nicknames.ask: Pages and Wikipedia say 'Spanish dancer' for either Hexabranchus species; H. lacer is the one mostly recorded in the Philippines (study 2.3).
'Blue dragon' often means Glaucus (not a Philippine reef slug) on general pages; Wikipedia's 'Blue Dragon' is not a sea slug.
No Wikipedia redirect; dive pages use it for Costasiella in general (study 4.2).

lookalikes.why: The two Spanish dancers: pages and Wikipedia say 'Spanish dancer' for either; WoRMS accepts both, citing Tibiriçá et al. 2023 (study 2.3, 6.3).

exclude.eggs: Egg ribbons and egg masses are never candidates (Pierre, 2026-11-15). (1) Drop an observation annotated with one of `annotations` ([iNaturalist term, value]: Life Stage: Egg; Evidence of Presence: Egg), read from the observation's own annotations: no request parameter removes them exactly. (2) Judging: drop a photo whose subject is an egg mass (ribbon, coil, rosette, capsules) with no whole animal recognisable, and a photo that cannot be told apart from one; the recognisable animal with its eggs beside it is judged as an animal photo; the observation's other photos stay (rule P4). Juveniles stay in. docs/reviews/2026-11-15-seaslug-sources.md 1.4.

photoTarget.juvenileRule: +5 only where a source documents a different-looking juvenile
